Install packages in a Conda environment

Source: R/install_packages.R
install_packages.Rd

Installs packages into an existing environment. install_packages() creates the default environment "condathis-env", empty, when it does not exist. Any other environment that does not exist aborts with class condathis_install_packages_env_not_found (also condathis_env_not_found). Create it with create_env() first.

Usage

install_packages(
  ...,
  env_name = "condathis-env",
  method = "auto",
  verbose = c("output", "silent", "cmd", "spinner", "full"),
  channels = "conda-forge",
  additional_channels = NULL,
  channel_priority = c("strict", "flexible", "disabled")
)

Arguments

...

Package match specs (MatchSpec strings) to install, unnamed: character strings or character vectors, in order. Examples: "python=3.13", "bioconda::samtools". At least one spec is required. No specs abort with class condathis_install_packages_missing_packages. Any other value aborts with class condathis_install_packages_invalid_packages. Such values are:

  • A named argument that install_packages() does not have. The error names the closest argument.

  • A value that is not a character vector.

  • NA or "".

  • A file name that ends in .yml or .yaml.

packages = <specs> still works. It is deprecated and warns once per session (class condathis_deprecated_packages_arg). install_packages() aborts with class condathis_install_packages_positional_env_name when env_name is not given and the last of two or more specs names an existing environment. Name the argument, as in env_name = "my-env". A spec that the backend cannot read, such as "::", aborts with class condathis_install_packages_failed. When the conda-meta/history of the environment records channels, condathis reads the specs first. Then such a spec aborts with class condathis_parse_match_spec_invalid_name. For the URL of a package file, the class is condathis_parse_match_spec_invalid_url. Both errors also have class condathis_invalid_arg.

env_name

Character string with the environment name. It must be a plain directory name that is valid on Linux, macOS and Windows:

  • Not empty, and not . or ...

  • Not starting with -, and not ending with ..

  • Without path separators, :, #, whitespace, control characters or <>"|?*.

  • Not a Windows device name, such as NUL or COM1 (see Environment names in create_env()).

Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_env_name. Functions that take only names reject an env_path() value with class condathis_env_path_read_only. run(), run_bin(), run_pipeline() and run_step() accept one.

method

Character string naming the backend. "auto" (the default) uses the backend that owns env_name when it exists, and otherwise the first available backend in getOption("condathis.backend_priority") order (see condathis-options). Any name from list_registered_backend_names() selects that backend, and "micromamba" is built in. The name of a backend whose package condathis knows, such as "rattler" of the rattlerthis package, also selects it. condathis loads the package on first use. It aborts with class condathis_backend_not_installed when the package is not installed. "native" is a deprecated alias for "micromamba" (warns once per session). If you name a backend other than the owner, functions that change the environment abort with class condathis_backend_mismatch. The others warn (condathis_backend_mismatch_warning) and use the owner. An environment found under several backends aborts with condathis_backend_ambiguous_env unless method names one of them. Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_method.

verbose

Character string that controls the console output. One of:

  • "output": show the output of the command and the messages of condathis.

  • "silent": show nothing.

  • "cmd": show the command line.

  • "spinner": show only a spinner.

  • "full": show the command line, the output, and the backend's own log.

TRUE means "output" and FALSE means "silent". Every level except "silent" shows a spinner in interactive sessions. Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_verbose (see condathis-conditions). The default is shown in Usage.

The command line shown, the cmd of a result and the messages of condathis show the password and the token of a URL as *****. micromamba does the same (https://user:*****@host/channel, https://host/t/*****/channel). The command still gets them.

channels

A non-empty character vector of channel names or URLs, in priority order. For a package from another channel, either name the channel in the spec ("bioconda::samtools") or add it here, as in channels = c("conda-forge", "bioconda"). Invalid values, such as NULL, NA or "", abort with class condathis_install_packages_invalid_channels. The conda-meta/history of the environment records the channels of its packages. When the call leaves out one of them, install_packages() warns with class condathis_install_packages_missing_previous_channels. Add that channel to channels or additional_channels. A channel named in a spec counts as included.

additional_channels

NULL (the default) or a non-empty character vector of channel names or URLs, used after channels. Invalid values abort with class condathis_install_packages_invalid_channels (also condathis_invalid_additional_channels).

channel_priority

Channel priority mode: "strict" (the default), "flexible" or "disabled", as in create_env(). Invalid values abort with class condathis_install_packages_invalid_channel_priority.

Value

A condathis_result object, invisibly: a classed list with status, stdout, stderr, timeout, pid, cmd and env_name. cmd is the command line that the backend ran, or NA when the backend reports none. stdout, stderr and pid are NA when the backend reports none, and pid always is with micromamba. A backend failure aborts with class condathis_install_packages_failed (also condathis_backend_error), with the backend's error as the parent. micromamba runs the link scripts of packages. A backend that does not makes install_packages() warn with class condathis_install_packages_link_scripts_skipped (also condathis_link_scripts_skipped). The warning names the packages.

Details

install_packages() installs packages for the platform of the environment, with every backend. That platform is the one the environment was created for (see platform in create_env()). Otherwise, on Apple Silicon and on Windows, it is the platform of the environment's packages that are not noarch. An environment with no packages other than noarch ones, such as a new "condathis-env", gets the emulation fallback of create_env() instead. Packages that cannot be installed for the native platform then use an emulated platform, when they can be installed there. That platform is "osx-64" on Apple Silicon when Rosetta 2 is running. On Windows with a backend that solves for "win-arm64", such as the win-arm64 micromamba, it is "win-64". Later installs then use the same platform.

Other R sessions

Only one R session at a time changes an environment. create_env(), install_packages() and remove_env() hold a lock on the environment name while they work, with every backend. A call for an environment that another R session is changing waits until that session is done. After two seconds, the call says so with a message of class condathis_env_lock_waiting. verbose = "silent" hides this message. Ctrl-C stops the wait. clean_cache() waits until no other R session creates an environment or installs packages. Those calls wait while it cleans. Each wait gives a message of class condathis_cache_lock_waiting. A lock lasts only as long as its session, also when the session crashes or is killed. The lock files are in the directory locks of the condathis data directory (see get_install_dir()). Where files cannot be locked, such as on some network file systems, the call goes on without the lock. When it changes something, it warns once per session with class condathis_env_lock_unavailable.

See also

condathis-conditions for every condition class.

Other environments: create_env(), env_exists(), env_path(), get_env_dir(), list_envs(), list_packages(), remove_env(), validate_env()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
condathis::with_sandbox_dir({
  # A local channel shipped with condathis, with `polyglot`: a
  # dependency-free script that runs on Linux, macOS and Windows.
  channel <- system.file(
    "extdata", "polyglot-channel",
    package = "condathis"
  )

  # Install `polyglot` into an existing, empty environment.
  condathis::create_env(env_name = "my-env")
  condathis::install_packages(
    "polyglot",
    env_name = "my-env",
    channels = channel
  )

  condathis::create_env(
    "bioconda::fastqc",
    env_name = "fastqc-env"
  )
  # Install the package `python` in the `fastqc-env` environment.
  # Keep unrelated tools in separate environments, so that their
  # dependencies cannot conflict.
  # `bioconda` is passed again, because `fastqc` came from it: leaving out
  # a channel the environment was built from warns. `conda-forge` comes
  # first: with strict channel priority, the first channel wins.
  condathis::install_packages(
    "python",
    env_name = "fastqc-env",
    channels = c("conda-forge", "bioconda")
  )
})
} # }
